stem: A 45-year-old man with a history of previous intravenous drug abuse presents to the hepatology clinic for follow-up of serology results and a liver biopsy for hepatitis C.He is found to have a genotype 4 hepatitis C virus, with a viral load800 000 and has early cirrhosis on liver biopsy. It is decided to treat him with the combination elbasvir/grazoprevir. Which of the following reflects the mode of action of elbasvir?
explanation: Elbasvir is an inhibitor of HCV NS5A, which is essential for viral RNA replication and virion assembly.

stem: A 29-year-old woman, who has used increasingly large amounts of cocaine over the past few months, comes to the Emergency Department suffering a panic attack. She is extremely anxious as she feels as if there are insects crawling under her skin. Over the past few months she has steadily increased the amount of cocaine that she is taking and is drinking half a bottle of whisky each evening to remain calm. On examination her BP is 155/90, with pulse 97 and regular. She is sweating and tremulous. Which of the following is the likely explanation for her skin sensations?
explanation: Haptic hallucinations are hallucinations involving skin sensation in the absence of stimuli, and are common in situations of alcohol withdrawal and stimulant drug overdose. In this situation medication with a benzodiazepine is the most appropriate intervention. Q.

stem: A 26-year-old woman with a history of alcoholism presents to the Emergency Department some 48h after an overdose of 20×500 mg paracetamol tablets. She has taken three previous overdoses and is well known to the hospital. On examination her BP is 110/80 and her pulse is 78 and regular. She is tender over the epigastrium and the right upper quadrant of the abdomen, which she attributes to vomiting. Which of the following is the most useful investigation with respect to prognosis?
explanation: Of all of the options listed above, it is prothrombin time that is most closely linked to outcomes. PT as expressed by INR2.0 at or before 48h or3.5 at or before 72 h drives referral to a specialist liver unit. Peak elevation occurs around 72?96 h. Kings College Hospital recommend listing for liver transplantation if PT is100(INR6.5), creatinine is300 μmol/l and there is grade II/IV hepatic encephalopathy all within a 24h period. Arterial pH7.3 or lactate3.0 are other criteria considered as drivers for referral/possible transplantation. Q.

stem: A52-year-old man with a history of hypertension and arthritis presents to the Emergency Department for the second time over the last six months with severe shortness of breath, periorbital swelling and tongue oedema. He is also hypotensive and is given subcutaneous adrenalin, and intravenous hydrocortisone and fluids. His medication history includes ramipril, amlodipine, ibuprofen, paracetamol and indapamide. Which of these medications is most likely to be the cause of his presentation?
explanation: This man is having episodes of angioedema and, out of the options given,ramipril is the likely culprit. It is important to remember that episodes may occur at any time after starting therapy,not necessarily within the first few weeks of initiation. Angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor therapy is responsible for 4-6% of cases of angioedema, and responds poorly to intervention. Discontinuing the medication is the most important next step. Q.

stem: A76-year-old woman is discharged to a nursing home for convalescence after a left hemi-arthroplasty following a fractured femoral neck.You are asked to make a domiciliary visit as she has become unwell. Over the past 48h she has suffered from watery diarrhoea, opening her bowels some six to eight times over the course of the day. Her BP is 115/80,with a postural drop of 20 mmHg. Her abdomen is soft with active bowel sounds, although there is some left-sided tenderness. Investigations reveal an elevated urea and stool is positive for Clostridium difficile toxin. Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention?
explanation: Both oral vancomycin and oral metronidazole are possible interventions for the treatment of C.dificile. It seems that, of the two, oral vancomycin achieves a slightly higher concentration in the mucosa as the diarrhoea resolves, compared to metronidazole, and is therefore associated with lower C.difficile recurrence rates. Q.

stem: A 65-year-old man presents to the Oncology Clinic for review. He is currently managed with a multi-agent chemotherapy regime for a haematological malignancy and complains of pains, predominantly in his feet, with loss of sensation. On examination, he has a peripheral sensory neuropathy affecting both feet. Which of the following agents is most likely to have been responsible?
explanation: Neuritic pain is seen first in patients with vincristine-related neuropathy. This is followed by sensory loss, paraesthesia, difficulty in walking, slap gait, loss of deep tendon reflexes, ataxia, paresis, foot drop and cranial nerve palsies, especially ocular palsies and laryngeal nerve paralysis. Therapy with vincristine should therefore be discontinued at this point. Q.

stem: A19-year-old woman presents to the Emergency Department with nausea, vomiting, a severe left-sided headache and facial weakness.This is the third episode of headache over the past 2 months, and she began the combined oral contraceptive pill some six months earlier. She takes no other regular medication and has no past medical history of note. On examination her BP is 148/88,with pulse 80 and regular. She is very anxious, neurological assessment confirming left-sided facial weakness. This weakness slowly resolves over 3 hours. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Oxygen card allowing her to present as an emergency to A&E
PRN sumatriptan for her next headache
explanation: This patient has developed migraine with weakness, associated with use of the OCP. Stopping the OCP is crucial because of the risk of progression to an ischaemic stroke. Q.

stem: A74-year-old man with a history of biventricular failure comes to the clinic for review.He complains of shortness of breath and decreased exercise tolerance, despite taking regular ramipril 10 mg, bisoprolol fumarate 10 mg,furosemide 40 mg and spironolactone 25mg. His blood pressure is 122/80 mmHg;his pulse is 85 bpm and regular.He has bilateral pitting oedema of both ankles and minor crackles at both lung bases. You plan to start him on ivabradine. Which of the following represents the mode of action of ivabradine?
explanation: The l,current controls spontaneous diastolic depolarisation in the sinus node and regulates heart rate. The cardiac effects are specific to the sinus node with no effect on intra-atrial, atrioventricular or intraventricular conduction times, nor on myocardial contractility or ventricular repolarisation. The l, current is present in the retina and is responsible for temporal resolution of vision. This may be partially inhibited by ivabradine leading to visual halo effects. Q.

stem: A 29-year-old woman with brittle asthma is admitted to the Emergency Department with a severe acute exacerbation. She has been admitted to the intensive care unit on two previous occasions in the past 18 months. Her peak flow on admission is 145(495 predicted). After 30 min of back-to-back salbutamol and ipratropium nebulisers, her peak flow has fallen to 135.There is poor air entry bilaterally with quiet wheeze. You plan to give her IV magnesium. Which of the following is an effect of magnesium in this situation?
explanation: Magnesium is given at a dose of 2 g IV for patients with acute severe asthma where there has been no response to nebuliser therapy and progression to intubation and ventilation is imminent. Even in patients who eventually require ventilator support,it may reduce their overall stay on the ITU/HDU. Magnesium is thought to inhibit smooth muscle contraction, decrease histamine release from mast cells and inhibit acetylcholine release. Q.

stem: A 25-year-old man comes to the Clinical Pharmacology Clinic for review. He has a history of familial hypercholesterolaemia, and despite maximal statin therapy,his total cholesterol is elevated at 6.9mmol/L. Clinical examination reveals both xanthelasma and arcus senilis. You elect to begin evolocumab therapy. Which of the following reflects the mode of action of evolocumab?
options: It is an agonist of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor a
explanation: Evolocumab is a proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9(PCSK9)inhibitor. It binds selectively to PCSK9.

stem: A72-year-old man is referred to the neurology clinic by his GP with possible Parkinson's disease. He has had no significant response to levodopa, and you are asked for advice on what to do next. He has not taken his medication on the day he attends the clinic.You note he has a shuffling gait as he walks into the clinic. His wife tells you that, in addition to deterioration in his walking, he has also had difficulties with short-term memory and urinary incontinence. On examination his BP is 148/90, with pulse 72 and regular.You note only mild rigidity, and no tremor on neurological assessment. He appears to have significant slowing of thought. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
explanation: The triad of gait disturbance, incontinence and memory loss is suggestive of normal pressure hydrocephalus. MRI or CT scanning may show ventricular enlargement out of proportion to sulcal atrophy and periventricular lucency, and is a logical next step before progression to lumbar puncture. Dificulty:Average.

stem: A 25-year-old man comes to the Oncology Clinic for review. He has completed treatment including excision of his right testis and intensive chemotherapy for a non-seminomatous germ cell tumour. Clinical examination is unremarkable;his surgical site has healed well and there is no evidence of lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is a useful tumour marker to monitor for recurrence?
explanation: Serum levels of alpha-fetoprotein and/or β-human chorionic gonadotropin are elevated in 80-85% of men with non-seminomatous germ cell tumours, even when non-metastatic. From the options given, it is therefore the most useful potential tumour marker. Difficuty.

stem: A 48-year-old female, diagnosed with breast cancer, believes that this was the result of an extra-marital affair that she had 10 years ago. She is awaiting surgery in the next few weeks. There is no significant past medical history apart from mild asthma, for which she has been taking a salbutamol inhaler. Examination apart from the left breast lump is entirely normal. Which of the following best describes the belief that her breast cancer is related to the affair?
explanation: This patient's fixed belief that her breast cancer is related to an extra-marital affair is clearly a delusion,an idiosyncratic belief or impression maintained despite being contradicted by reality or rational argument.

stem: A 32-year-old woman comes to the Diabetes Clinic for review. She has recently been admitted for the third time in the past seven months with diabetic ketoacidosis. This is despite having attended the DAFNE(Dose Adjustment for Normal Eating) course and modulating her insulin dose according to carbohydrate intake and level of exercise. She is becoming increasingly depressed. Current therapy includes basal bolus insulin and ramipril 2.5mg started after she developed microalbuminuria six years earlier. Her blood pressure is 123/72 mmHg;her pulse is 72 bpm and regular;her body mass index is 21 kg/m.Thereis 1+ of protein on the urine dipstick and the most recent glycated haemoglobin(HbAc) is 77 mmol/mol (9.2%). Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Arrange a 72-hours continuous glucose monitoring system assessment
Reassure her that things will improve
Refer her for insulin pump therapy
explanation: Difficulty.

stem: A 65-year-old house painter is admitted after fainting at work for the second timein the last few months. He tells you that he has been feeling progressively dizzier when he paints. He is left-handed. Past history of note includes hypertension and a previous inferior myocardial infarction. He smokes 20 cigarettes per week. On examination, his blood pressure is 155/90 mmHg; his pulse is 78 bpm and regular. There are no murmurs. His chest is clear. His abdomen is soft and non-tender, and his body mass index is 24kg/m. You suspect he may have subclavian steal syndrome. Which of the following is a direct branch of the left subclavian artery?
explanation: Difficulty.

stem: A 29-year-old man is started on varenicline for smoking cessation. He is intrigued by the data on its central effects and wants to know how it works. What is the mechanism of action for varenicline?
explanation: Varenicline binds with high affinity and selectivity at the a4β2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, where it acts as a partial agonist-a compound that has both agonist activity, with lower intrinsic efficacy than nicotine, and antagonist activity in the presence of nicotine. Its use is associated with four-week quit rates40% versus 17% for placebo. Difficuty.

stem: A51-year-old woman comes to the clinic for review. She has a history of type 2 diabetes and is currently treated with metformin 1g twice daily. Since beginning therapy, she has experienced a 2kg fall in her weight and a 0.7% reduction in her glycated haemoglobin(HbA1c).On examination, her blood pressure is 132/82mmHg; her pulse is 65bpm and regular. Her body mass index is 30kg/m. Which of the following is the mode of action of metformin?
explanation: AMP kinase activation stimulates hepatic fatty acid oxidation, ketogenesis, skeletal muscle fatty acid oxidation and glucose uptake. It inhibits cholesterol synthesis, lipogenesis and triglyceride synthesis, and adipocyte lipolysis and lipogenesis. Metformin is an indirect activator of AMP kinase. Difficuty.

Over the past three months, he has developed burning pain which keeps him from sleep every night, affecting both feet.
